title: Sharp stability for the (B)-theorem
summary: The (B)-theorem of Cordero-Erausquin, Fradelizi and Maurey states that if $γ$ is the standard Gaussian in $\mathbb R^n$, $K \subset \mathbb R^n$ is an origin-symmetric convex set, and $s, t \in \mathbb R$ then $γ\left(e^{\frac{s + t}{2}} K\right) \ge \sqrt{γ(e^{s} K) γ(e^{t} K)}$. Herscovici, Livshyts, Rotem and Volberg proved a stability version of this result, showing that if one has equality up to a factor $(1 + ε)$ in the (B)-inequality for $K$ then the inradius of $K$ must be either ``very large'' or ``very small,'' where the bounds depend on $ε$ and on $n$.
